analysis.title: Nobody want the AI boom in their backyard
key_insights: Political backlash is emerging as a constraint on the AI data center buildout. Morgan Stanley warns a Democratic midterm sweep could threaten the buildout, with Texas the main flashpoint.
BofA's Hartnett cites a survey in which 76% of voters oppose new data centers in their communities.
Morgan Stanley sees Texas as the biggest political risk. The newly elected Democratic governor has advocated a moratorium on new data center approvals.
Texas grid interconnection requests have reached 474 GW, more than five times the state's record peak electricity demand. The note says many requests may be speculative.
Goldman raised its 2030 global data center capacity estimate from 217 GW to 273 GW and its US estimate from 125 GW to 152 GW. That is about 170 GW of additional global capacity after 2025.
Goldman acknowledges growing risks from power constraints, regulation and leverage but still expects large expansion.
Morgan Stanley says slower data center construction could reduce AI-related corporate debt issuance, which could ease long-duration bond supply and support longer-dated Treasury prices.

Morgan Stanley argues that restrictions on new construction could benefit existing facilities with secured power connections through scarcity value and pricing power. EQIX and DLR are named as established operators that could benefit, while speculative developers relying on future approvals face more uncertainty.
